name: Acute Kidney Injury
remarks: Models recurrent, sporadic episodes of acute kidney injury (AKI) in adults.
The pre-fix module rolled a flat 22% AKI risk once, 1-10 years after birth --
concentrating essentially all AKI in early childhood, which does not reflect
reality (AKI risk rises steeply with age and is driven by acute illness,
nephrotoxic exposure, and comorbidity, not childhood per se). This version
drops that pediatric roll entirely: an 18+ Guard gates entry, then an
annual age-banded incidence loop runs for the rest of the patient's life,
so AKI can recur.
Annual incidence: 0.4%/yr at 65+, 0.05%/yr for adults 18-64. Order-of-
magnitude source: Hsu CY, McCulloch CE, Fan D, Ordonez JD, Chertow GM, Go
AS. 'Community-based incidence of acute renal failure.' Kidney Int.
2007;72(2):208-212 -- overall creatinine-defined community AKI incidence
around 1/1000 person-years, rising sharply with age into the several-per-
1000 range at 65+; the bands here are consistent with that gradient.
Severity (Assess_AKI_Severity) is read from the `creatinine` attribute
drawn at AKI_Creatinine_Value/-Check: <2.0 mg/dL mild, <4.0 moderate,
>=4.0 severe. The >=4.0 mg/dL severe threshold intentionally coincides
with the KDIGO Stage 3 absolute-creatinine criterion (KDIGO Clinical
Practice Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury, Kidney Int Suppl.
2012;2(1):1-138), which is reused at AKI_Outcome to gate mortality.
Mortality is attributed only to severe (KDIGO Stage 3-equivalent)
episodes, ~15%, via the Death state. Order-of-magnitude source: Hoste
EAJ, Bagshaw SM, Bellomo R, et al. 'Epidemiology of acute kidney injury
in critically ill patients: the multinational AKI-EPI study.' Intensive
Care Med. 2015;41(8):1411-1423 -- hospital mortality rises steeply by
KDIGO stage, with Stage 3 mortality in the ~15-30% range depending on
care setting; 15% is used as a conservative point estimate spanning ward
and ICU severe AKI. Moderate episodes are not modelled as directly
fatal. Post-AKI progression to CKD is also stratified by severity,
consistent with Coca SG, Singanamala S, Parikh CR. 'Chronic kidney
disease after acute kidney injury: a systematic review and meta-
analysis.' Kidney Int. 2012;81(5):442-448 (pooled CKD risk after AKI is
substantial and rises with AKI severity).
Recovered episodes close the acute condition (ConditionEnd, 7-90 days
after the acute encounter) and loop back into the annual incidence
check, so a patient can experience multiple discrete AKI episodes over
a lifetime.
Fix round 1: fixing the Observation.assign_to_attribute drop above made
Assess_AKI_Severity's severity gate live for the first time, which
exposed that the original uniform 1.2-6.5 creatinine draw sent 47% of
episodes to Severe_AKI/Dialysis (real AKI RRT ~2-6%). AKI_Creatinine_Value
is now a distributed_transition into three banded draws (see its own
remarks) so P(creatinine >=4.0, severe) ~= 13%, within the 10-15% target.
This module does not attempt to model pediatric AKI (see module
remarks); block entry to the annual incidence loop until adulthood.
Annual timer and router in one state (see the pneumonia.json module
for the same idiom): the Delay must elapse before the
complex_transition rolls, and a no-onset roll (or a recovered
episode's ConditionEnd) re-enters this same state, allowing repeat
AKI episodes across a patient's adult life.
0.4%/yr at 65+, 0.05%/yr for ages 18-64 -- see module remarks for
sourcing.
Fix round 1: the original single uniform 1.2-6.5 draw made
Assess_AKI_Severity's severity gate (previously inert -- see below)
route 47% of episodes to Severe_AKI/Dialysis once the
Observation.assign_to_attribute silent-drop bug was fixed, against a
real AKI RRT rate of ~2-6%. Reshaped right-skewed via a
distributed_transition into three banded draws so P(creatinine
>=4.0, i.e. severe/KDIGO-Stage-3-equivalent) ~= 13%, in the 10-15%
range the controller targeted (creatinine >=4.0 mg/dL routes every
episode to Dialysis in this simplified model, so this also bounds
the dialysis rate). Band shares approximate the KDIGO-stage mix
reported for hospitalised/community AKI (most episodes are mild;
severe/Stage-3-equivalent is a minority): KDIGO Clinical Practice
Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury, Kidney Int Suppl. 2012;2(1):1-138
for the staging definitions, and Hoste EAJ, Bagshaw SM, Bellomo R,
et al., Intensive Care Med. 2015;41(8):1411-1423 (AKI-EPI) for the
order-of-magnitude stage distribution -- that cohort is ICU-only and
skews sicker (~19% Stage 3) than this module's general hospital/
community population, so 13% (toward the low end of the
controller's 10-15% band) is used here.
Draw the severity-determining value into an attribute first, then
have the Observation read it back via `attribute` (not
`assign_to_attribute`, which the engine silently drops on Observation
states -- see task-1.10-report.md and this task's controller notes).
Assess_AKI_Severity, AKI_Hospital_Disposition, and AKI_Outcome all
read this same `creatinine` attribute downstream.

codes.display: Urea nitrogen [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma

remarks: Route on the same `creatinine` >= 4.0 mg/dL threshold used to send
patients to Severe_AKI / Dialysis -- this module's stand-in for
KDIGO Stage 3. Only that branch carries mortality risk.
~15% mortality, higher CKD progression than moderate AKI. See
module remarks (Hoste et al. 2015; Coca et al. 2012) for sourcing.
No direct mortality modelled for moderate (non-Stage-3-equivalent)
AKI; some CKD progression risk remains. See module remarks (Coca et
al. 2012) for sourcing.
Task 2.11 (sweep, P3b review finding): AKI_Outcome_Severe/Moderate
previously routed straight into Progress_to_CKD/CKD_Lisinopril with
no open encounter -- Nephrology_Followup_End had already closed the
last one, and AKI_Monitoring (7-21 day Delay) elapses in between, so
HealthRecord.currentEncounter() silently re-attached the new CKD
diagnosis and the lisinopril order to that stale, already-closed
follow-up encounter instead of throwing. This wraps both in their
own visit, reusing the same follow-up encounter code as
Nephrology_Followup above.
Task 2.11 (sweep, P3b review finding): the CKD-progression arm never
reached AKI_ConditionEnd, so Acute kidney injury (14669001) stayed
active in HealthRecord.present forever for every patient who
progressed to CKD -- concurrently with the new Chronic kidney
disease diagnosis below, which is what progression to CKD actually
means clinically. A dedicated state (rather than routing through
the existing AKI_ConditionEnd) because that one's own
direct_transition is AKI_Annual_Check, the recovery-arm's re-entry
point into the annual recurrence loop -- reusing it here would skip
Progress_to_CKD/CKD_Lisinopril entirely. This module's post-CKD
loop-back behavior (CKD_Lisinopril -> Terminal, not back into
AKI_Annual_Check) is unchanged; only the missing condition-end and
encounter wrap are in scope here.
Task 2.11 (sweep): had none of codes/condition_onset/
referenced_by_attribute -- null cause of death for every AKI death.
condition_onset (not referenced_by_attribute) because AKI_Diagnosis
has no assign_to_attribute; safe from the renamed-entry null-cause
trap (State.Death.process, condition_onset form) because 14669001
is not ConditionOnset'd by any other state tree-wide (grep-
verified), so nothing can overwrite the shared present-map entry's
name away from 'AKI_Diagnosis'. AKI_Diagnosis dominates this state
(verified by dominator analysis).
